findings.title: A Call from IT Support Leaves a Company at the Mercy of Hackers: National Police Chief Reveals Details of Cybercriminal Gang That Made Over $40 Million
findings.summary_md: Ukraine's Cyberpolice and National Police published the account of a two-year joint investigation with the FBI. Acting police chief Maksym Tsutskiridze said the group built a platform with AI-generated voice messages, called employees posing as IT support and persuaded them to hand over credentials or install remote-access software before stealing data and encrypting files. He said at least 28 companies had paid more than $40.5 million, about UAH 1.8 billion, and described one US victim that lost 1.4 TB of data, was asked for $10 million and paid $5 million after negotiation. The release says four key suspects were charged and detained after 66 searches, with almost $370,000 and EUR 20,000 in cash seized.

findings.title: Ukraine and the FBI expose a hacker network extorting over $40 million
findings.summary_md: UNN reported the Prosecutor General's Office account of an international organization exposed with the FBI, with at least 27 members from Ukraine, Kazakhstan and Russia and a linked network of more than 60 people across eight jurisdictions that included former Conti members. At least 28 companies were identified as having paid more than $40.5 million, with final damages still being established. The report says the group impersonated IT support staff to obtain credentials and install remote-access software, used AI to automate calls, and demanded cryptocurrency while threatening to publish stolen data. It also reports 66 searches in Kyiv and 11 regions and the seizure of $370,000 and EUR 20,000 in cash.

findings.title: Офіс генпрокурора та ФБР викрили міжнародне хакерське угруповання, арештовано 4 ключових учасників
findings.summary_md: Interfax-Ukraine reported that Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office and the FBI exposed an international criminal organization that attacked foreign companies for multimillion-dollar ransoms. It cites at least 27 members from several countries and a linked network of more than 60 participants in eight jurisdictions, including former Conti members. Four key suspects were served with suspicion notices under Part 2 of Article 255 and Part 5 of Article 361 of Ukraine's Criminal Code and remanded in custody, facing up to 15 years. The report says 28 companies had paid over $40.5 million, and that 66 searches in Kyiv and 11 regions seized computers, phones, bank cards, almost $370,000 and EUR 20,000.

findings.title: Ukraine and US authorities uncover international ransomware network linked to former Conti hackers
findings.summary_md: H.ua reported that Ukrainian police and the FBI uncovered a transnational group that used AI-assisted calls and ransomware to steal data and block large enterprises, with documented ransom payments exceeding $40.5 million, or about UAH 1.8 billion. Attackers posed as IT support staff, obtained credentials, persuaded employees to install remote-access software and automated fraudulent calls with AI before encrypting files and threatening to leak them. In one case they took 1.4 TB from a US company, demanded $10 million and received $5 million after negotiation. The article says four suspects were detained under Articles 255(2) and 361(5) of Ukraine's Criminal Code after 66 searches and face up to 15 years in prison.

findings.title: The National Police and the FBI have uncovered hackers demanding a $40 million ransom
findings.summary_md: UkrMedia reported that Ukrainian law enforcement and the FBI uncovered a hacking group that attacked corporate networks, stole data and demanded multimillion-dollar ransoms. At least 28 companies paid more than $40.5 million, about UAH 1.8 billion, and the group used AI-generated voice messages while calling staff as technical support. The report describes 66 simultaneous searches in Kyiv and 11 regions, four detentions and seizures of computers, phones, bank cards, nearly $370,000 and EUR 20,000. It says the organization had at least 27 members, a broader network of more than 60 people in eight jurisdictions including former Conti members, and one US victim that lost 1.4 TB and paid $5 million against a $10 million demand.
